name: George Clinton
hook: The Parliament-Funkadelic bandleader's own 1982 solo hit became the sample gangsta rap built a whole sound out of.
blurb: Royalty and copyright disputes with Bridgeport Music, and PolyGram's takeover of Casablanca, made the old band set-up unworkable, and in 1981 George Clinton had to dissolve Parliament and Funkadelic. He signed to Capitol Records as a solo artist. His 1982 single 'Atomic Dog', from the album 'Computer Games', is credited to Clinton alone, and it reached number one on the R&B chart on its own, separate from either band's catalogue. A decade later its chant, 'bow wow wow, yippee yo, yippee yay', became one of the most sampled pieces of music in West Coast hip-hop and a foundation of G-funk. Dr. Dre's production, especially on 'The Chronic' (1992), treats P-Funk's music in general, and 'Atomic Dog' in particular, as a starting point for the sound rather than an occasional source.
